key_insight: A biologically informed dual-branch transformer separates intrinsic cell state from drug-induced regulatory shifts to accurately predict transcriptional responses across doses and times, allowing strong generalization to unseen cellular contexts.
problem_solved: Predicting how cells' transcriptional programs change after drug treatment is hard because responses mix baseline cell identity with dose- and time-dependent perturbations; this model disentangles those factors to produce accurate, generalizable predictions.
method: Dual-branch transformer architecture: one branch encodes baseline cell state, the other encodes drug-induced regulatory perturbations, with learned fusion to predict post-perturbation transcription.
Biologically informed priors: incorporate pathway/regulatory structure (e.g., gene modules or network constraints) to guide attention and improve interpretability and robustness.
Dose–time modeling: explicit representation of nonlinear dose and time dynamics so the model can predict continuous perturbation trajectories and generalize to unseen conditions.
impact: Enables more accurate, interpretable in silico prediction of drug responses and improves transfer to new cell types or conditions—useful for ML practitioners building models for perturbation biology, drug screening, and hypothesis generation.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing two transformer branches (cell state vs drug perturbation) and a fusion head producing predicted expression

Bar/line chart comparing generalization performance on seen vs unseen cell contexts
paper_title: Modelling drug-induced cellular perturbation responses with a biologically informed dual-branch transformer
paper_authors: Yue Guo, Hao Zhang, Haitao Hu, Jialu Wu, Ji Cao
